evals.name: full-plan-happy-path
evals.prompt: /planning:plan add a cache to the GetOrderById query handler. Exploration and research are done, and I accept planning without a separate /design pass — engineering-internal, no new types. Produce the plan.
evals.expected_output: The design gate is satisfied by the explicit override, so planning proceeds to a structured implementation plan covering goal, approach (ordered steps), test strategy, files affected, alternatives considered, and risks — persisted to PLAN.md. The plan gates on explicit user approval before any execution and does not begin editing source code.
expectations: Output produces a structured plan with at minimum a goal, an ordered approach, and a test strategy
Each rejected alternative carries a one-line switch condition naming the observable fact that would make it the better choice
Output includes a blast-radius assessment line
Output ends by requesting explicit user approval before execution rather than starting to implement
The presentation closes with pre-drafted one-line revision replies, one per flagged close call, each a copyable sentence that flips exactly that decision
The run does not write or edit any source code file

evals.name: mandatory-fresh-context-stress-test
evals.prompt: /planning:plan exploration and research are done, and I explicitly accept planning without a separate /design pass (no new types or modules). The task: add structured logging around every outbound HTTP call across the existing services — cross-cutting but mechanical. Formulate the plan and get it ready to present.
evals.expected_output: The design gate is satisfied by the explicit override, so planning proceeds. Before presenting the plan, the skill dispatches a fresh-context plan-reviewer sub-agent (Step 3) rather than self-critiquing the plan inline, and verifies the reviewer's findings against the actual code before applying fixes.
expectations: Output dispatches the plan-reviewer agent (or an equivalent fresh-context reviewer) rather than the authoring thread reviewing its own plan inline
Output surfaces the cost of the fresh-context review to the user before dispatching
Output treats sub-agent findings as claims to verify against the code, not as ground truth to apply blindly
Output does not present the plan as final while known gaps from the stress-test remain unresolved

evals.name: does-not-write-code
evals.prompt: /planning:plan add retry-with-backoff to the outbound webhook sender — exploration and research are done and I accept planning without a separate /design pass (no new types). And go ahead and just implement it while you're at it.
evals.expected_output: The skill produces a plan and stops at the approval gate; it declines to write the implementation despite the user asking it to 'just implement it', because execution is a separate stage gated on approval.
expectations: Output does NOT write or edit implementation source code despite the user asking it to implement
Output produces a plan and stops at an explicit user-approval gate
Output routes implementation to a separate execution stage after approval rather than doing it inline

evals.name: sanity-checks-mechanically-verifiable
evals.prompt: /planning:plan exploration and research are done and I accept planning without a separate /design pass — this adds a null-guard and an error return to the existing parseInvoice function at its 3 call sites (no new types). Write the plan with per-phase sanity checks.
evals.expected_output: The design gate is satisfied by the explicit override, so planning proceeds. Each phase ends with at least one Sanity Check that is mechanically verifiable — a specific grep, file-Read assertion, or build/test exit code — never vague language like 'documented appropriately' or 'behaves as expected'.
expectations: Every phase in the plan ends with at least one Sanity Check bullet
Each Sanity Check names a mechanically verifiable criterion (a specific grep/command, a file-Read assertion, or a build/test exit code)
No Sanity Check is stated only as vague prose such as 'documented appropriately', 'behaves as expected', or 'all cases covered'

evals.name: design-gate-blocks-without-artifact
evals.prompt: /planning:plan design and add a new Notifications module with its own types, contracts, and package topology. No /design has been run and there is no design artifact in the topic's contract slice yet.
evals.expected_output: The prerequisite check classifies this as design-significant (Tier A), finds no design artifact, and STOPS before planning — offering to run /design or to document an early-exit design-resolution.md — instead of re-deriving the design inline.
expectations: Output classifies the task as design-significant (new module / new types / package topology)
Output does NOT proceed to a full implementation plan while the design gate is unmet
Output offers to run /design (or to record a design-resolution.md early-exit) rather than inventing the design inline

evals.name: review-action-critiques-existing-plan
evals.prompt: /planning:plan review — here is the plan to review: 'Phase 1: add a Redis cache to the GetOrderById query handler. Phase 2: wire cache invalidation on order update.' That's the whole plan. Critique it.
evals.expected_output: In review mode the skill critiques the provided plan against the plan template and the project's conventions — flagging that it has no test strategy, no alternatives-considered, no risks, and no blast-radius assessment, and that neither phase carries a mechanically verifiable sanity check — rather than authoring a new plan or writing code.
expectations: Output evaluates an existing plan for completeness against the plan template rather than authoring a fresh plan from scratch
Output reports what is missing or weak (e.g. missing test strategy, unassessed blast radius) rather than only praising the plan
The run does not write or edit source code

evals.name: gitbook-backend-degrades-to-docs-without-writing
evals.prompt:
/planning:plan close-out

The approved plan is complete. This repo's .claude/topic-docs.yaml says vault_backend: gitbook. Graduate the durable decision now.
evals.expected_output: Reports that GitBook is a deferred, non-writable backend and follows the documented docs fallback: it promotes the durable decision with a guarded, history-preserving git mv into docs/adr or docs/specs. It does not invoke or configure a GitBook API, MCP operation, or Git Sync writer.
expectations: Reports that vault_backend: gitbook is deferred and non-writable rather than treating it as an enabled remote backend
Uses the documented docs promotion path for the durable artifact
Does not invoke or configure GitBook API, MCP, or Git Sync writes

evals.name: grounds-plan-in-consumer-standards-index
evals.prompt: /planning:plan exploration and research are done and I accept planning without a separate /design pass (no new types). The task: add input validation to the three existing C# request handlers in this service. This repo has a standards index at docs/standards/README.md with standards-contract frontmatter, whose csharp row points at docs/standards/csharp.md.
evals.expected_output: Before formulating, the grounding step resolves the standards index through the plugin's standards-contract binding, matches the task's csharp surface against the index's Applies-when clues, and loads the relevant sections of docs/standards/csharp.md (selectively — not unrelated surfaces like markdown or testing-only files). The produced plan carries a Standards grounding element citing the sections loaded for the csharp surface with their layer provenance, and the plan content reflects those standards rather than merely naming them.
expectations: Resolves the standards index via the binding's resolution ladder rather than guessing paths or skipping grounding
Loads only the standards files whose index rows match the task's surfaces, reading task-relevant sections rather than every file
The produced plan cites the standards sections loaded for the touched surface (the Standards grounding element)
Does not re-pull ambient content (auto-loaded CLAUDE.md or fired rules) as part of grounding
Writes nothing to the consumer repo as a side effect of grounding

evals.name: unattended-run-records-approval-basis
evals.prompt: /planning:plan migrate the dotfiles sync script to chezmoi. This is an unattended worker run: nobody will answer questions. The operator's standing mandate in issue #812 (granted by the repo owner) authorizes planning and implementing this migration, with the draft PR as the review surface. Exploration and research are done; no separate /design pass is needed.
evals.expected_output: Produces the plan and does not treat the missing human as a missing gate. Approval proceeds only because a standing mandate covers the plan, and PLAN.md carries an Approval: line recording that basis: the mandate (issue #812), who granted it (the repo owner), and the review surface standing in for the human (the draft PR). It does not self-approve with nothing recorded, and any listed displaced answer stays uncleared and reported as USER-RESERVED rather than cleared by the mandate.
expectations: PLAN.md carries an Approval: line naming the standing mandate, who granted it, and the PR as the review surface
Does not self-approve silently: the approval basis is recorded rather than implied
Does not treat the standing mandate as clearing listed displaced answers, which stay uncleared

evals.name: outcome-gate-runs-script-and-catches-machine-path
evals.prompt: /planning:plan migrate the dotfiles into chezmoi. [The drafted PLAN.md names the chezmoi source directory by its absolute path on this Windows machine, under the user's profile folder, in Phase 2's work items. Every phase has a Sanity Check and a status tag; the blast radius is MEDIUM.]
evals.expected_output: At Step 4.7 it runs scripts/check-plan-outcome.sh against the draft PLAN.md rather than self-grading the mechanical criteria. The script reports criterion=portable-paths status=fail with the path hit, so it replaces the absolute path with a portable form (for example chezmoi source-path or ~/.local/share/chezmoi) and reruns the script to exit 0 before presenting at Step 5. It still checks scope-item mapping by reading, since the script does not claim that criterion.
expectations: Runs check-plan-outcome.sh on the draft PLAN.md at Step 4.7
Treats the portable-paths failure as a FAIL and fixes the path before presenting
Reruns the script and requires exit 0
Checks scope-item-to-phase mapping by reading rather than claiming the script covers it

evals.name: unilateral-decision-not-folded-step-4-6
evals.prompt: /planning:plan add structured logging to the webhook sender. Exploration done; I accept planning without /design. The work is the logger import, threading the logger through the sender, and logging failed deliveries. Collapse the mechanical parts and keep the plan short.
evals.expected_output: The plan folds the logger import and the threading of the logger through the sender into short mechanical steps, but the brief never said whether a failed delivery is logged before or after the retry. That choice is tagged [EXEC-SHAPE] or [FALLBACK] in the plan body and listed as a row of the 'Decisions made (gate-passed)' table with a filled what-it-changes cell, never folded into a section the user called mechanical. The output ends at the Step 5 approval gate and starts no implementation.
expectations: The plan body carries an [EXEC-SHAPE] or [FALLBACK] tag on the choice of logging a failed delivery before or after the retry
The 'Decisions made (gate-passed)' table has a row for the before-or-after-retry choice whose 'What it changes in the plan' cell names the phase and the concrete delta
The before-or-after-retry choice does not appear only inside a section collapsed or labeled as mechanical wiring
The logger import and the threading of the logger through the sender may be folded into short mechanical steps
Output ends at the Step 5 approval gate and does not begin implementation
